items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: we were replacing the orchestra of Arthur Gibbs at 7 o'clock for one hour while they had dinner.

ctx.x: When the girl had finished dancing with the other fellow, I invited her to dance and when we got on the floor, I offered her the ticket, she was surprised and must have thought that I was really a dumb one. She told me that tickets were only necessary when a man danced with a girl that was hired for that purpose. I felt ashamed that after one dance I made an excuse to leave the floor and never saw the girl again.

Then came the great day of our tryout for the job. The matinee started at 4 in the afternoon on the 24th December 1927 and we were replacing the orchestra of Arthur Gibbs at 7 o'clock for one hour while they had dinner. That was alternating with Fess for one hour and then with Gibbs for another hour.

Before coming to New York we had uniforms made by a mail order place and when we received them in Springfield, none of us had a perfect fit. But it was a uniform made of Oxford grey cloth with a black band around the collar and lapel of the coat and the same band around the side of the pants. We bought green checkered ties to go with the costume.
